newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major says will not hold election after May 1.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major says will not hold election after May 1.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major said on Thursday he would not hold an election later than May 1.
"I won't go beyond May 1," he said on Sky Television. "I have a date in my mind yes, but we'll see how events will unroll and I will make an announcement."
Major said a meeting with cabinet ministers on Thursday morning had not discussed possible election dates.
"I think people should just sit back and relax and not get overexcited about it for the moment," he said. The election must be held by May 22.
The prime minister dismissed suggestions that a vote next Monday on the government's handling of the mad cow crisis could bring his administration down.
The opposition Labour Party has launched a bid to sack Britain's agriculture minister, Douglas Hogg, by calling a parliamentary debate on his actions over mad cow disease.
If Labour wins the debate, Hogg would be forced to resign and a vote of no-confidence in Major's Conservative administration could be triggered later in the week.
"We haven't got a crisis on Monday, we have got a stunt from the Labour Party," Major said. "I expect to win on Monday."
He said he would not do deals with the nine Ulster Unionist MPs who generally support the government but are angry about the mad cow crisis.
"I'm not in the business of doing miscellaneous deals that aren't in the interests of good government generally," Major said.
